title: Elephant Shoes, the new romantic comedy musical from @Two River Theat...
transcript: I just experienced one of the most innovative and creative new musicals I've seen in years, and it's just a train ride away from New York City. This summer, there are so many cool new shows happening outside of New York, and I've made it my mission to see as many as possible. So I started in New Jersey at the world premiere of Elephant Shoes, a new musical at Two River Theatre. This is a co production with Deaf West, a groundbreaking theater company where deaf and hearing artists share the stage and accessibility is part of the storytelling. This was my first Deaf West production, and I was so excited to see it, and I've genuinely never seen anything quite like Elephant Shoes. The musical is performed in both American Sign Language and spoken English, and every moment of the show is either signed, spoken, or projected in text, or a combination of the three. It's beautiful to watch. The staging is incredibly inventive, and it's just a very entertaining show. Elephant Shoes is a modern adaptation of Cyrano de Bergerac, but it's a romantic comedy. Instead of Cyrano being a man with a big nose, his name is Sai, and he is deaf. The cast is so fantastic, especially Daniel Durant, who plays Sai. You might know him from the film Koda or Devdas or dancing with the stars. He's just such a compelling actor and is so ridiculously charming. And then his Roxanne and question are Roxy and Chris Played by Taylor Montgomery Jones and James Oliva, and they just have great chemistry, and the show has so much heart. I'm just so happy I got to see this delightful, romantic musical. And if you live in New York City, it could not be easier to get to. It is the perfect day trip. It's currently only running through the end of June. Go, go, go and see it.
